explanation_full: This correlation heatmap visually shows how related different chemical measurements are to each other. The closer the numbers are to 1 (or -1), the stronger the relationship, meaning that when one measurement changes, the other tends to change in a predictable way. For example, the strongest relationship shown is between Butyrate and VFA, with a correlation of 0.9601, indicating they tend to increase and decrease together. When looking at the relationship with Hydrogen Production Rate (HPR), VFA (0.7984) and Butyrate (0.7827) show the strongest positive correlations, suggesting that higher levels of these compounds are associated with higher HPR. A practical caution is that correlation does not prove causation; while these features are strongly related to HPR, other unmeasured factors might be the true cause.
